title: (No AI) Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Qualcomm logo over a multicolored illustration](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24007992/acastro_STK082_qualcomm_02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

With smartphone sales [tanking by around 20 percent](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/1009588/global-smartphone-sales-just-hit-a-14-year-low) compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its [Q4 2026 earnings](https://investor.qualcomm.com/files/content_files/FY2026-4th-Quarter-Earnings-Presentation_Final.pdf) call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like [Amazon](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/991372/qualcomms-collaborating-with-amazon-on-multiple-generations-of-chips-for-aws-data-centers) and [Meta](https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/2026/06/qualcomm-and-meta-announce-strategic-multi-generation-agreement-) announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.

Considering the company's [total revenue](https://investor.qualcomm.com/files/content_files/FY2026-4th-Quarter-Earnings-Release.pdf) for 2026 was $10.4 billion, …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1026867/qualcomm-earnings-data-centers)

title: (No AI) 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
author: Elizabeth Lopatto
content:
![Elon Musk frowns, surrounded by all the things he could have bought and didn’t](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/268859_How_the_tech_right_could_have_spent_all_the_money_they_burned_on_the_midterms_CVirginia.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Dream bigger, babe. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty Images

One of the basic problems of spending too much time on social media is that you are cooking your brain by reading posts from [a pack of attention-seeking lunatics](https://www.theverge.com/24058356/trolls-social-media-commenter-lurker-reply-guy-threads). If your social media of choice is the site formerly known as Twitter, and [it is your main source of contact with the outside world](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-025-06187-8), you may delusionally throw away nearly $500 million dollars on midterm elections, just like Elon Musk.

In particular, $47 million of that money from Musk's America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico, who trounced Musk's preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, with 55 percent of the vote. Talarico even made Musk's influence [a cent …](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/james-talarico-campaign-ad-elon-musk-texas-senate-election.html)

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1026878/not-even-good-at-being-rich)
